reviewed_sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
reviewed_sources.supported_claim: A governance model can define roles, responsibilities, policy, oversight, risk priorities, and review cycles.
reviewed_sources.limitations: The CSF governs cybersecurity risk, not marketing automation. Any use in the article must be labeled as an operating-governance analogy, not a NIST marketing standard.

supported_claims: Governance can use explicit roles, responsibilities, policy, oversight, risk prioritization, and recurring review.

drafting_constraints: Label NIST CSF 2.0 as a governance analogy rather than a marketing-automation standard.

briefs.approval_notes: Approved with constraints; NIST supports governance principles, not a marketing automation mandate.

reviewed_sources.title: CAN-SPAM Act: A Compliance Guide for Business
reviewed_sources.supported_claim: U.S. commercial email is subject to sender-identification, truthful-message, address, opt-out, and compliance-monitoring requirements described by the FTC.
reviewed_sources.limitations: U.S. federal guidance only; it is not legal advice and does not replace jurisdiction-specific review. Penalty amounts and legal requirements must be rechecked before publication.

reviewed_sources.title: Email sender guidelines
reviewed_sources.supported_claim: Gmail documents authentication, subscription, unsubscribe, formatting, and monitoring requirements for mail sent to personal Gmail accounts.
reviewed_sources.limitations: Gmail-specific and time-sensitive; sender-volume thresholds, enforcement, and technical requirements must be rechecked before publication.

supported_claims: Retention email operations should account for truthful sender/message information, unsubscribe handling, authentication, recipient expectations, and ongoing monitoring.
unsupported_claims: Universal legal compliance, deliverability guarantees, fixed optimal cadence, or any claim that a retention workflow guarantees repeat purchases.
drafting_constraints: Do not provide legal advice; tell readers to verify rules for every applicable jurisdiction.
Distinguish commercial, subscription, and transactional messages without declaring a reader's legal classification.
Treat Gmail requirements as provider-specific and time-sensitive.
Avoid deliverability, engagement, revenue, and retention benchmarks.
briefs.approval_notes: Approved with legal and platform constraints based on current FTC and Gmail guidance.
